reading.review:
Jane Austen's sharpest social comedy remains astonishingly fresh more than two centuries later. Elizabeth Bennet's quick wit and Mr. Darcy's slow, earned humility turn a story of manners and marriage into a study of self-knowledge.

Every secondary character — from the pompous Mr. Collins to the dryly detached Mr. Bennet — lands with effortless comic timing.

note.note-text: Iconic opening line setting up the ironic tone of the entire novel.
Darcy's letter at Hunsford marks the structural pivot where Elizabeth confronts her own misjudgments.
